title: Zechariah Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Zechariah chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Zechariah Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Zechariah Chapter 13.

questions.question: In Zechariah 13, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: A fountain opened to the house of David
Cutting off the names of idols
Prophets and unclean spirits passing out of the land
Father and mother thrusting through their son
questions.correctAnswer: A fountain opened to the house of David
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned in Zechariah 13 is the opening of a fountain for sin and uncleanness, found in Zechariah 13:1.

questions.question: What shall be opened to the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
options: A fountain for sin and uncleanness
questions.correctAnswer: A fountain for sin and uncleanness
questions.explanation: According to Zechariah 13:1, a fountain is opened for sin and uncleanness.

questions.question: What will the Lord of hosts cut off from the land?
questions.correctAnswer: The names of the idols
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:2 states that the Lord will cut off the names of the idols from the land.

questions.question: What will no longer be remembered according to Zechariah 13:2?
questions.correctAnswer: The idols
questions.explanation: As mentioned in Zechariah 13:2, the names of the idols shall no more be remembered.

questions.question: What will happen to the prophets and unclean spirits in Zechariah 13?
options: They will pass out of the land
questions.correctAnswer: They will pass out of the land
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:2 indicates that the Lord will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land.

questions.question: What will happen if someone prophesies according to Zechariah 13:3?
options: They will be thrust through by their parents
questions.correctAnswer: They will be thrust through by their parents
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:3 states that if someone prophesies, their parents will thrust them through for speaking lies in the name of the LORD.

questions.question: Who will say 'Thou shalt not live' to the prophet in Zechariah 13:3?
questions.correctAnswer: His father and mother
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 13:3, it is stated that the father and mother that begat him shall say unto him, 'Thou shalt not live.'

questions.question: What is the reason given in Zechariah 13:3 for the parents' actions towards the prophet?
options: He speaks lies in the name of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He speaks lies in the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:3 states that the parents will act against their child because he speaks lies in the name of the LORD.

questions.question: In Zechariah 13:2, who declares the actions regarding idols and prophets?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD of hosts
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:2 begins with 'And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD of hosts,' indicating that it is the LORD of hosts who declares the actions.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 13:1, the fountain is opened for what?
questions.correctAnswer: Sin and uncleanness
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:1 specifies that the fountain is opened for sin and uncleanness.

questions.question: The actions described in Zechariah 13 are said to take place in which day?
questions.correctAnswer: The day of the LORD
questions.explanation: Both Zechariah 13:1 and 13:2 mention 'in that day,' referring to the day of the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: A fountain is opened to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:1 states that there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: The idols will be remembered in that day.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:2 indicates that the names of the idols shall no more be remembered.

questions.question: True or False: The parents will support their child's prophecy.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:3 states that the parents will thrust their child through for prophesying, indicating they will not support him.

questions.question: True or False: The unclean spirit will be honored in the land.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:2 states that the unclean spirit will pass out of the land, not be honored.

medium.title: Zechariah Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Zechariah Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to the prophets in that day according to Zechariah 13:4?
options: They will be ashamed of their visions
questions.correctAnswer: They will be ashamed of their visions
questions.explanation: The verse states that the prophets shall be ashamed of their visions, indicating a recognition of false prophecies. (Zechariah 13:4)

questions.question: What does Zechariah 13:2 promise will happen if idols are cut off from the land?
options: Prophets and unclean spirits will pass out of the land
There will be no more sin
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets and unclean spirits will pass out of the land
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:2 states that the LORD will cut off the names of idols and cause the prophets and unclean spirit to pass out of the land, signifying a purification process.

questions.question: What profession does the man in Zechariah 13:5 claim to have?
questions.correctAnswer: An husbandman
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 13:5, the man states, 'I am no prophet, I am an husbandman,' indicating his humble profession as a farmer.

questions.question: What consequence does Zechariah 13:3 describe for someone who prophesies lies?
options: They will be punished by their family
questions.correctAnswer: They will be punished by their family
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:3 indicates that if someone prophesies lies in the name of the LORD, their parents will thrust them through, demonstrating the severe consequences of false prophecy.

questions.question: What question is asked regarding the wounds in the man's hands in Zechariah 13:6?
options: What are these wounds in thine hands?
questions.correctAnswer: What are these wounds in thine hands?
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:6 states that one shall ask the man about the wounds in his hands, highlighting a curiosity about his suffering.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 13:4, what will the prophets not wear to deceive?
questions.correctAnswer: Rough garments
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:4 specifies that the prophets shall not wear a rough garment to deceive, indicating a rejection of false appearances.

questions.question: What does the fountain opened in Zechariah 13:1 signify?
options: A means for cleansing from sin
questions.correctAnswer: A means for cleansing from sin
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:1 states that the fountain opened is for sin and uncleanness, indicating its purpose of spiritual cleansing.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 13:5 reveal about the man's upbringing?
options: He was taught to be a prophet
He was taught to keep cattle
He was raised in a wealthy family
questions.correctAnswer: He was taught to keep cattle
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'man taught me to keep cattle from my youth,' indicating his background in agriculture rather than prophecy.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 13:2 indicate will happen to the unclean spirit?
questions.correctAnswer: It will be cast out
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:2 mentions that the LORD will cause the unclean spirit to pass out of the land, indicating its removal.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 13:6 indicate about the man's wounds?
options: They were given in the house of friends
questions.correctAnswer: They were given in the house of friends
questions.explanation: The man responds that the wounds were those with which he was wounded in the house of his friends, suggesting betrayal or harm from close associates.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 13:3, what will happen to the false prophet?
options: They will be killed by their parents
questions.correctAnswer: They will be killed by their parents
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:3 describes a severe consequence where the parents will thrust through their child for prophesying lies, showing the gravity of false prophecy.

questions.question: The statement 'I am no prophet' reflects what about the man's identity in Zechariah 13:5?
questions.correctAnswer: He is humble
questions.explanation: By stating 'I am no prophet,' the man displays humility and a rejection of false claims to prophetic identity. (Zechariah 13:5)

questions.question: Does Zechariah 13:4 imply that prophets will continue to deceive?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:4 indicates that prophets will be ashamed and will not wear garments to deceive, implying an end to their deception.

questions.question: Does Zechariah 13:1 promise a cleansing for the people of Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:1 states that a fountain will be opened for sin and uncleanness, indicating a promise of cleansing for the people.

questions.question: Is it true that the false prophets will be praised according to Zechariah 13:3?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:3 states that false prophets will face severe consequences, not praise, indicating the seriousness of their actions.

hard.title: Zechariah Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Zechariah Chapter 13.

questions.question: In Zechariah 13:7, what is the consequence mentioned after the shepherd is smitten?
questions.correctAnswer: The sheep shall be scattered
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:7 states, 'smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered,' indicating the scattering of the sheep as the consequence of the shepherd being smitten.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 13:8, what fraction of the land's inhabitants shall be left after two parts are cut off and die?
questions.correctAnswer: One third
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:8 says, 'two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein,' showing that one third remains.

questions.question: In Zechariah 13:9, how does the LORD describe the refining process of the third part?
options: As silver is refined and gold is tried
As wheat is sifted and bread is baked
As oil is pressed and wine is poured
As stones are polished and jewels set
questions.correctAnswer: As silver is refined and gold is tried
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:9 states, 'I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried,' describing the refining process.

questions.question: Who is called upon by the refined third part in Zechariah 13:9, and what is the LORD's response?
options: They shall call on my name, and I will hear them
They shall call on the kings, and kings will hear them
They shall call on the prophets, and the prophets will answer
They shall call on their ancestors, and the ancestors will guide them
questions.correctAnswer: They shall call on my name, and I will hear them
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:9 clearly states, 'they shall call on my name, and I will hear them,' affirming the LORD's attentive response.

questions.question: In Zechariah 13:7, who does the LORD call 'my fellow' along with 'my shepherd'?
options: The man that is my fellow
The prophet that is my servant
The king that is my anointed
The priest that is my servant
questions.correctAnswer: The man that is my fellow
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:7 says, 'Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, and against the man that is my fellow,' identifying the two as related figures.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 13:9 indicate the refined people will say about the LORD?
options: The LORD is a mighty warrior
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is my God
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:9 states, 'I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The LORD is my God,' showing their confession.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'ra'ah' (רָעָה) used in Zechariah 13:7 typically mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Shepherd
questions.explanation: In Zechariah 13:7, 'ra'ah' means 'shepherd,' referring to a leader or caretaker, consistent with its common usage in Hebrew.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Zechariah 13:7-9, where the shepherd is smitten and the sheep scattered, followed by refinement of the remnant?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The passage uses a chiasm structure, contrasting the smitten shepherd and scattered sheep with the refining and preservation of a remnant, a common Hebrew literary technique.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of a shepherd being struck and the sheep scattering as in Zechariah 13:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 26:31
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:31 quotes Jesus saying, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered,' directly referencing Zechariah 13:7.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with the refining of the remnant by fire as mentioned in Zechariah 13:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Malachi 3:3
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:3 describes the LORD refining and purifying like silver and gold, paralleling Zechariah 13:9's refining theme.

questions.question: What immediately precedes Zechariah 13:7 in the chapter?
options: A description of wounds in the hands from friends
The fountain opened for sin and uncleanness
The cutting off of idols from the land
questions.correctAnswer: A description of wounds in the hands from friends
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:6 precedes 13:7 and mentions, 'Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends,' setting the context for the shepherd's suffering.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 13:2 foreshadow the purification theme developed in verses 7-9?
options: By declaring the removal of idols and unclean spirits from the land
By describing the construction of a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: By declaring the removal of idols and unclean spirits from the land
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:2 states that the names of idols and unclean spirits will be cut off, initiating the purification that culminates in the refining of the remnant in later verses.

questions.question: What typological role does 'the shepherd' in Zechariah 13:7 play in Christian theology?
options: A foreshadowing of Jesus Christ as the Good Shepherd
questions.correctAnswer: A foreshadowing of Jesus Christ as the Good Shepherd
questions.explanation: Christian theology often sees the shepherd smitten in Zechariah 13:7 as a type of Christ, the Good Shepherd who is struck and whose sheep are scattered, fulfilled in the New Testament.

questions.question: What literary parallelism is present in Zechariah 13:9 between refining metals and God's trial of His people?
options: Synonymous parallelism, equating silver refining and gold trying with spiritual purification
Antithetic parallelism, contrasting fire and water
Synthetic parallelism, developing a new thought about judgment
Emblematic parallelism, comparing people to trees
questions.correctAnswer: Synonymous parallelism, equating silver refining and gold trying with spiritual purification
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:9 uses synonymous parallelism by paralleling refining silver and trying gold as metaphors for God's purifying of His people.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 13:3 describes a scenario where a prophet's own parents reject him for prophesying lies.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:3 states that a prophet's parents say, 'Thou shalt not live; for thou speakest lies in the name of the LORD,' confirming parental rejection.

theological.title: Zechariah Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Zechariah Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Zechariah 13:1 teach about God’s provision for human sin?
options: God provides a cleansing fountain for sin and uncleanness
God ignores human sin and uncleanness
God punishes sin without provision for cleansing
God allows uncleanness to remain as a test
questions.correctAnswer: God provides a cleansing fountain for sin and uncleanness
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:1 states that 'In that day there shall be a fountain opened... for sin and for uncleanness,' teaching the doctrine of divine provision for cleansing from sin.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning idolatry and false prophecy is taught in Zechariah 13:2?
options: God will completely remove idolatry and false prophecy from the land
God tolerates idolatry as a cultural norm
False prophets will be exalted among the people
Idolatry and false prophecy are necessary evils
questions.correctAnswer: God will completely remove idolatry and false prophecy from the land
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:2 explains that God will 'cut off the names of the idols' and cause 'the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land,' affirming total removal of idolatry and false prophecy.

questions.question: What doctrine about prophetic authenticity and familial rejection does Zechariah 13:3 present?
options: True prophets will face rejection even from their own families
Prophets will be universally honored by their families
Families are responsible for protecting false prophets
Prophecy is always accepted without question
questions.correctAnswer: True prophets will face rejection even from their own families
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:3 describes how a prophet’s own parents will say 'Thou shalt not live' because he speaks lies in God's name, indicating the doctrine that genuine prophetic witness may bring familial rejection.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Zechariah 13:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:7 shows God commanding the sword to smite the shepherd, demonstrating divine sovereignty over life and death and the unfolding of redemptive events.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Zechariah 13:9 by God refining His people?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:9 describes God refining the people 'as silver is refined,' highlighting His holiness and the sanctifying work He performs on His people.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 13:1 connect to the theme of atonement in the broader biblical narrative?
options: It anticipates the cleansing work of the Messiah
It denies any need for atonement
It teaches atonement through ritual sacrifices only
It focuses solely on national restoration without spiritual cleansing
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the cleansing work of the Messiah
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:1’s fountain opened for sin and uncleanness prefigures the Messianic atonement that cleanses from sin, aligning with the broader biblical theme of salvation through Christ.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Zechariah 13:7 make with New Testament fulfillment?
options: It prophetically depicts the shepherd’s suffering and the scattering of the sheep, fulfilled in Jesus’ crucifixion and the disciples’ scattering
It predicts the restoration of Israel without suffering
It forbids any harm coming to the shepherd
It suggests the shepherd will conquer militarily without sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: It prophetically depicts the shepherd’s suffering and the scattering of the sheep, fulfilled in Jesus’ crucifixion and the disciples’ scattering
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:7’s call to smite the shepherd and scatter the sheep anticipates Jesus’ death and the apostolic dispersal, connecting Old Testament prophecy with New Testament events.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Zechariah 13:2 and Zechariah 13:4 teach about false prophecy and divine judgment?
options: False prophecy will be exposed and judged, leading to shame and removal from the land
False prophets will be rewarded and encouraged
False prophecy is acceptable as long as it promotes peace
questions.correctAnswer: False prophecy will be exposed and judged, leading to shame and removal from the land
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:2 promises removal of false prophets and unclean spirits, and 13:4 shows prophets ashamed of their visions, teaching that false prophecy faces divine judgment and disgrace.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is taught by the combination of Zechariah 13:8 and Zechariah 13:9?
options: God purifies His people through trials, leaving a refined remnant
All people will be saved without testing
Judgment is final without opportunity for refinement
Sanctification is an instantaneous event without process
questions.correctAnswer: God purifies His people through trials, leaving a refined remnant
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:8 speaks of two-thirds being cut off but a third refined by fire in 13:9, illustrating sanctification as a refining process by God.

questions.question: What theological synthesis do Zechariah 13:5 and Zechariah 13:6 provide about the identity and suffering of the true prophet?
options: The true prophet may deny his office and bear wounds from persecution among friends
The true prophet always openly claims his office without suffering
The true prophet is free from any physical or social suffering
The true prophet’s wounds are from his enemies only
questions.correctAnswer: The true prophet may deny his office and bear wounds from persecution among friends
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:5 shows the prophet denying being a prophet, claiming to be a husbandman, and 13:6 speaks of wounds received 'in the house of my friends,' indicating suffering and denial.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Zechariah 13:7-9 teaches God arbitrarily punishes the faithful. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God’s judgment includes refining trials that purify and preserve a faithful remnant
God abandons His people without hope
God’s judgment is random and unexplainable
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment includes refining trials that purify and preserve a faithful remnant
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:7-9 reveals that while many suffer judgment, God refines a third part, demonstrating purposeful sanctification rather than arbitrary punishment.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s judgment is taught in Zechariah 13:8?
options: Divine judgment will be severe but allow for a preserved remnant
God’s judgment is universal destruction without exception
Judgment is only symbolic with no real consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Divine judgment will be severe but allow for a preserved remnant
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:8 states that two parts will die and one part will be left, teaching that God’s judgment is severe yet merciful in preserving a remnant.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is underscored in Zechariah 13:2 by God’s action against idols and false prophets?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: By cutting off idols and false prophets, God demonstrates His holiness and intolerance of sin as shown in Zechariah 13:2.

questions.question: What theological lesson about human sin and divine cleansing is drawn from Zechariah 13:1 and 13:9 together?
options: God provides cleansing from sin and purifies His people through trials
Sin remains unaddressed and people remain unclean
Cleansing is only external with no internal transformation
God’s cleansing is temporary and incomplete
questions.correctAnswer: God provides cleansing from sin and purifies His people through trials
questions.explanation: Zechariah 13:1 promises a fountain for cleansing sin, while 13:9 describes refining the people, teaching comprehensive cleansing and sanctification by God.

questions.question: How do Zechariah 13:3 and 13:4 together teach about the social cost of true prophecy in a fallen world?
options: True prophets face rejection and shame even from close relations
True prophets are always celebrated and honored
Prophecy involves no risk or social consequence
Prophets control political power and safety
questions.correctAnswer: True prophets face rejection and shame even from close relations
questions.explanation: Verse 13:3 describes familial rejection and 13:4 shows prophets ashamed, indicating the social cost of true prophetic ministry.
